blocks.html: Google RCS Business Messaging replaces the plain-text alert from an unknown number with a branded, interactive message that lands inside the same app a customer already uses to text friends. Built on Google's RCS infrastructure and the GSMA's Universal Profile standard, it lets a verified business send rich cards, carousels and tappable buttons without asking anyone to install a new app.

This guide covers how it actually works, what a verified sender profile gets you, real cost components, and where it fits next to the SMS and WhatsApp channels you're probably already running. sections.heading: Which Phones and Carriers Actually Support It

blocks.html: RCS runs on Android 5.0 and above through Google Messages or a carrier's own messaging app, and Apple added native support starting with iOS 18 — so a growing share of iPhone users can now receive verified business messages too. In India, coverage runs through Jio, Airtel and Vi at the network level, and a message simply drops to standard SMS whenever a device, carrier or connection doesn't support the richer format, so reach never actually shrinks.

items.q: What is Google RCS Business Messaging?
items.a: It's the business layer built on Google's RCS infrastructure and the GSMA's Universal Profile standard. A verified business sends branded rich cards, carousels and quick-reply buttons directly inside a customer's default messaging app, with no separate app to install.

items.q: How does Google RCS Business Messaging work for customer communication?
items.a: A verified sender profile sits behind every message, a rich card carries the images, text and buttons, and a customer's tap or reply feeds straight back into the same thread — including handoff to a chatbot or a live agent when needed.

items.q: How do I get verified as a Google RCS sender?
items.a: You submit business details, a logo and identity documents through an RCS provider to Google's Business Messages console, Google reviews the submission, and you test in a sandbox before going live. Ojiva AI runs this process directly with clients rather than leaving it as a self-serve form.

items.q: Is Google RCS Business Messaging secure enough for OTPs and payments?
items.a: Business messages are secured in transit and carry a verified sender identity, though they aren't end-to-end encrypted the way personal RCS chats are. For OTPs and payment prompts, that verified branding is what makes a code trustworthy at a glance, and every send falls back to SMS if a device can't receive the rich version.

items.q: How much does RCS business messaging cost?
items.a: Pricing usually combines a platform subscription with a per-message fee for rich cards, plus SMS fallback billed separately and applicable GST. There's no single flat rate — ask any provider for an actual rate card against your expected volume.

items.q: Can businesses reach iPhone users with RCS?
items.a: Yes. Apple added native RCS support starting with iOS 18, so verified business messages now reach a growing share of iPhone users, with automatic SMS fallback covering any device that isn't ready yet.

items.q: Does RCS automatically fall back to SMS?
items.a: Yes — whenever a device, carrier or connection doesn't support the richer format, the same message drops to standard SMS automatically, so delivery isn't lost.

items.q: What's the difference between RCS and WhatsApp Business API?
items.a: RCS runs inside a phone's native messaging app with no install required, while WhatsApp only reaches customers who already have the app. The two overlap heavily on features — rich media, buttons, verified branding — and most businesses run both rather than picking one.
